definition.name: close_gripper
definition.description:
Close the selected gripper.
Use when: the jaws are positioned around what you intend to hold, or another close is useful; repeat a close only after a fresh observation.
Effect: runs one committed sequence through the Supervisor and consumes one robot decision: close (close the gripper), on the arm you name; the other arm is not commanded. It dispatches at most 1 primitive action; the Supervisor admits every one like the matching atomic command. The end-effector pose target is held unchanged.
Returns: a submitted acknowledgement now, with target_ref echoed under intent labelled agent_annotation_only; on the next turn a staged receipt with one entry per stage that ran (status, reason, measurements), the stages not reached, and a fresh observation.
Does not: require segmentation or check the target_ref annotation against anything; establish contact, attachment, retention or task success; report jaw separation; a closed jaw is not a grasp.
On error: Refused: an argument outside this schema (invalid_arguments, naming the field); another committed sequence is still running (skill_sequence_active); a placement is waiting at its pre-release stop (skill_sequence_paused); the episode has reached its terminal boundary (episode_terminal). A refusal submits nothing: correct the named field, or act on current evidence, before calling again.

arm.description: The arm that runs the whole sequence. The other arm is not commanded and holds its current targets.

rationale.description: One short sentence saying why you chose this action now, at most 200 characters. It is echoed into the receipt and is the only record of the reason: the trajectory keeps the call and its result, never the reasoning behind them.

target_ref.description: What you believe the jaws are closing on. Optional; echoed as an agent annotation, never resolved or measured.

claim_boundary: submitted is not executed: the staged receipt on the next turn reports what each stage did, and no stage outcome certifies task success
